# Genomes {#sec-genomes}

::: {.callout-note title="From the exam description"}
Fundamental differences in how different genomes are constructed. What is
the difference between eukaryotic and prokaryotic genomes?
:::

## Introduction

::: {.callout-warning title="To be written"}
Short introduction: genome size and gene content across the tree of life;
operons vs. split genes; non-coding DNA, repeats and transposons;
chromosomes and 3D organisation; pan-genomes.
:::

## Key concepts

- Genome size, gene number and gene density across bacteria, archaea and eukaryotes; the C-value paradox
- Prokaryotic genome organisation: circular chromosomes, operons, plasmids, compact genomes, GC skew
- Eukaryotic genome organisation: introns and splicing, alternative splicing, large intergenic regions, centromeres/telomeres
- Repeats and transposable elements; segmental duplications
- Non-coding RNAs and regulatory elements; what fraction is "functional" (ENCODE debate)
- Organelle genomes and endosymbiosis
- Pan-genomes: core vs. accessory genes; horizontal gene transfer
- 3D genome organisation: chromatin, TADs (Hi-C)
- Population-genetic explanations of genome complexity (Lynch)

## Key papers

### Reviews — start here

- @koonin2008 — genomics of bacteria and archaea: the emerging dynamic view of the prokaryotic world.
- @lynch2003 — the origins of genome complexity.
- @koonin2011 — are there laws of genome evolution?

### Landmark genomes

- @fleischmann1995 — the first complete genome of a free-living organism (*Haemophilus influenzae*).
- @lander2001 — the public human genome draft.
- @venter2001 — the Celera human genome.
- @nurk2022 — the complete human genome.

### Genome function and organisation

- @encode2012 — ENCODE: an integrated encyclopedia of DNA elements.
- @liebermanaiden2009 — Hi-C: the 3D organisation of the human genome.
- @tettelin2005 — the microbial pan-genome.
- @treangen2011 — horizontal gene transfer in prokaryotes.
